moments.title: Wright finishes the Robie House
moments.text: Frank Lloyd Wright designed the long, low brick house for businessman Frederick C. Robie in 1908 and 1909, and it was finished in 1910. It became the best-known example of his Prairie style.

moments.title: First demolition threat
moments.text: The Chicago Theological Seminary, which owned the house, announced plans to tear it down for a dormitory. A letter-writing campaign, joined by Wright, stopped it.

moments.title: Wright, at 90, fights to save it
moments.text: When the seminary again planned to raze the house, Wright visited to draw attention to the threat. A development firm then bought the house as part of Hyde Park urban renewal.

moments.title: The university takes over
moments.text: The University of Chicago took on the house and promised to preserve it, and it was designated a National Historic Landmark the same year.

moments.title: Restoration finished
moments.text: An $11 million restoration, begun on the exterior in 2002, was completed.

moments.title: A UNESCO World Heritage Site
moments.text: The Robie House and seven other Wright buildings were listed together as The 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright.

moments.title: Today: the Frederick C. Robie House museum
moments.text: The Frank Lloyd Wright Trust runs tours of the house on the University of Chicago campus.

checked.notes: Completed 1910 (designed 1908 to 1909); demolition threats in 1941 and 1957 by the Chicago Theological Seminary; bought by Webb & Knapp as part of Hyde Park urban renewal; University of Chicago took responsibility in Feb 1963; NHL 1963 (University of Chicago, NPS, Wikipedia). $11 million restoration finished Mar 2019; UNESCO listing 2019 with seven other Wright works.
